notes:
Payroll correctness release. Includes Windows x64 NSIS + MSI installers and Tauri updater artifacts (latest.json + signatures).

**Fixes to amounts**
- Loan balances now drop by exactly what the payslip deducted. Before, when net pay was too small to cover every installment, balances dropped by the full installment anyway.
- Re-running payroll for an open month no longer deducts loans twice.
- Payslips are always calculated and stored by the app itself. If anything changed since the preview (salary, loans, an employee), you will be asked to upload the timesheet again instead of saving outdated figures.
- A blank "days worked" cell in a timesheet is now reported as an error. Before, it was read as 0 days, which deducted the whole month's pay.

**Protection for posted months**
- Posted months, and the salary records their payslips used, can no longer be changed or deleted, even outside the app.
- A failed payroll run or import leaves nothing half-saved.
- A legacy import never changes a posted month, and leaves a month open if any of its rows failed.

**Automatic updates**
- The app now checks for new versions on start (and every few hours) and shows "New version is available" to every user. One click downloads the update, installs it and restarts the app. Users on 1.0.2 get this release through the existing "Check for updates" button or by running the installer.

**Other changes**
- The on-screen payslip now shows the full breakdown, including each allowance, matching the PDF.
- Clearer errors for invalid data, such as zero hours per day, more than 30 days worked, unreadable amounts, or the same employee listed twice.
- Security (cloud mode): the app no longer contains the server's administrator key. Every request uses the signed-in user's own session, so the installer no longer gives anyone administrator access to the cloud data. Users sign in as before.

**Before you update**
- The database is upgraded automatically on first start. Any data that was previously read as 0 without warning (for example, an amount stored as text) now produces an error naming the field, so it can be corrected.
- Cloud mode: deploy the updated Worker and apply its database migration (`npm run cf:migrate:remote`) before users update.
